chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about shortening the prayer. He said, 'In a Bair.' I said, 'What is a Bair?' He said, 'Indeed, if he travels a Bair and returns a Bair, it occupies his day.'

key_terms.بَرِيدٍ: Bair (a unit of distance, approx. 8-9 km)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Bair distance for shortening prayer in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that the threshold for traveler's prayer (Qasr) is defined by the distance of 'Bair' (approximately 8-9 km), specifically when one travels this distance and returns within the same day. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the practical definition of travel duration and distance as the primary criteria for legal concessions, distinguishing it from mere proximity to the city limits.
